text: 🇲🇽🌎 "An embassy is like a small piece of your territory." "An embassy is like a small piece of [our] territory." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on relations with Ecuador In April 2024 Ecuadorian police stormed Mexico's embassy in Quito to seize a former vice president who had been granted asylum — a breach of the Vienna Convention. Mexico cut ties. Asked about restoring them, Sheinbaum was open to dialogue but firm on the principle Ecuador broke.

🚨🇲🇽 "What proof do they have?" "The people this statement names were already under investigation by our Financial Intelligence Unit. They rushed ahead with their announcement — they didn't wait for joint coordination. What proof do they have?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on new US Treasury sanctions Washington sanctioned Mexican individuals and companies unilaterally, without informing Mexico. Cooperation, yes — subordination, no.

🇲🇽🎨 A free public university for history, feminism, and popular resistance. "[A model] to form students with solid academic preparation, critical thinking and social conscience — through public, free, quality education." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the new INEHRM The new institute opens degrees in History and Public Administration, and master's programs in Mexican Humanism, Gender Studies and Feminisms, and Social Movements. Free diploma courses cover migration, popular resistance, human rights, and AI & the humanities.

🇲🇽🎨 "History is part of the living memory of a people." "History is not a catalogue of dates nor a succession of illustrious names. History is part of the living memory of a people." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, signing the INEHRM decree The decree turns the Institute of Historical Studies of Mexico's Revolutions into a research and teaching body under the Science and Humanities Secretariat. History as a living tool of the people — not a shelf of bronze statues.

🇲🇽✊ Eight years ago today, the people won. "Eight years ago was the triumph of the Fourth Transformation of Mexico's public life — July 1st. And the way to honor it, the triumph of the people, is this Institute dedicated to history." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, on the 8th anniversary of the 4T On July 1, 2018, Mexico elected AMLO and began the Fourth Transformation. Eight years on, Sheinbaum marked the date by signing a decree that turns the national historical-research institute into a public university.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICAN EXPORTS JUMP 25.4% — HIGHEST MAY ON RECORD, FIVE STRAIGHT MONTHS OF GROWTH

INEGI reports exports hit 69.5 billion dollars in May, up 25.4% year-on-year — the strongest May since records began — with non-oil, non-auto manufacturing up 38%. The trade balance stayed in surplus at 2.26 billion dollars, and the first five months of 2026 close at a 5.77 billion dollar surplus, against just 918 million in the same period last year. The "tariffs will crush Mexico" narrative keeps running into the data and losing.

🇲🇽💧 RECORD RAIN, NO CHAOS — MEXICO CITY'S WATER SYSTEM ABSORBED ITS BIGGEST STORM OF THE ADMINISTRATION

June 28 brought the heaviest rainfall of the entire administration: 42 million cubic meters of water over Mexico City alone, 73 million across the metro area, 8.3% above the previous record. Segiagua chief Mario Esparza credits the "Tlaloque 2.0" drainage system and new hydraulic works for keeping flooding down and the city moving. This is what public infrastructure looks like when it is built to serve people rather than sold off — doing exactly the job it was made for on the worst day of the year.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO'S GOVERNMENT IS INVESTIGATING ITS OWN — WHY MEDICINE FOR A CHILDREN'S HOSPITAL WAS LEFT TO EXPIRE

The Anti-Corruption and Good Government Secretariat has opened an investigation into why medicines, medical devices and supplies destined for the Hospital Infantil de México were allowed to accumulate and expire, and it will determine responsibilities. Notice what is actually happening here: the state is auditing itself, out loud, at the morning press conference — not burying the file. Under the old regime an expired-medicine scandal vanished into a drawer; now it becomes a public investigation.

🇲🇽📚 MEXICO TURNS ITS HISTORY INSTITUTE INTO A FREE PUBLIC UNIVERSITY — AND POINTS IT AT THE GLOBAL FAR RIGHT

Sheinbaum signed a decree today converting the INEHRM into a decentralized public institute of research and teaching, offering free degrees, master's programs and diplomas: bachelor's in History, in Social Sciences and Humanities, and in Public Administration and Good Governance, plus master's in Mexican Humanism, Gender Studies and Feminisms, and Rescue of Historical Memory. One research line is written into the decree — the advance of the far right around the world. Director Felipe Ávila says the institute will convene Latin American critical thinkers to study it, and will put classics of history and social science online for free, some translated into Indigenous languages and turned into audiobooks. "Education is a right, not a commodity."

LATIN TIMES: Cartel Drones Carrying Explosives Mark New Concern Near Texas Border
July 1, 2026 | 🔴

📰 A "new concern" that recycles drone-fear reporting already circulating since February. The one documented cartel drone bombing this cycle hit a state prosecutor's office in Tijuana — a Mexican target, inside Mexico. 🔍

Framed as a menace creeping toward Texas; the actual victims of cartel drones have been Mexican police and communities, not the US border.
